business_scope: Seasonal price trends, Bahar-based market timing, export window analysis, and marketing strategies for pomegranates in India.

crop_business_factors.details: Pomegranate realisations fluctuate heavily based on Bahar selection. Fruit harvested during low-supply windows, such as festival seasons (Diwali) or specific export windows, fetch up to 40% higher rates per quintal compared to peak harvest gluts.
Clean skin finish, deep red aril color, and uniform sizing determine whether fruit captures lucrative Middle Eastern and European export channels or lower local mandi prices.

common_risks.details: Failure to meet strict residue limits or quality grading standards results in cargo rejection and forced domestic dumping at depressed prices.

market_factors.details: Consumer demand peaks during major cultural and religious festival periods, driving sharp wholesale price spikes for grade-A fruit.

cost_factors: Sorting, grading, and specialized export packaging materials
Cold-chain transport and air/sea freight logistics
revenue_factors: Proportion of fruit qualifying for premium size and color brackets
cost_revenue_factors.important_rule: Pomegranate market profitability depends entirely on synchronizing the harvest window with high-demand festival or export periods.

strengths: High international demand and premium pricing for top-grade Bhagwa.
weaknesses: Perishable nature with short shelf-life without immediate cold storage.
opportunities: Expanding direct-to-retail and export supply chain linkages.
threats: Intense global competition and localized unseasonal rain damage.

things_to_monitor: International export demand indices and freight rates
Domestic festival calendar alignment with harvest maturity
Skin finish quality and sizing distribution
